question: Do public SRSF1 supplements provide reference predictions and exact sample joins that narrow the previously reported replay and chronology gaps?
prior_information: Published article conclusions, 292 gene coefficients, an intercept, two library adjustments, 72 human factor-off sample records, and the unresolved GEO 8/16 versus caption 6/12 timing discrepancy were already known. Workbook descriptions are visible; workbook numeric values have not been inspected for this audit.
inputs: current author code and publisher text
scope: Inventory every sheet, dimensions, formula presence, column labels and sample-identifying fields.
Extract explicitly labeled published prediction/reference rows and their units, preserving source workbook/sheet/cell coordinates.

Join only exact sample/library identifiers to the existing GEO/count-column manifest. A donor/group/time match without an individual sample key remains group-level provenance, not a unique library join.
Report exact, missing, duplicate and ambiguous joins; preserve all failed rows.
Reconcile timing labels only when an explicit primary-source sample-level mapping establishes equivalence. Do not infer calendar dates from effect values.
Audit current and newly found code dependencies without executing author scripts or deserializing models.
If a complete documented preprocessing path and paired reference input/output become available, submit a separate frozen replay contract before applying the clock to counts.
no_outcome_selection: No sample subset will be chosen by prediction direction or magnitude. Published reference values are not independently reproduced biological ages. No new treatment-effect p-values or calibrated safety/state labels will be computed.

claims.verified: Source extraction, exact identities and numerical bookkeeping only
claims.heuristic: Biological interpretation of published age estimates

determinism: Pin SHA-256 for downloaded workbooks and prior manifest before numeric extraction. Deterministic outputs exclude retrieval timestamps.
